# Rathlin Island

Rathlin Island is Northern Ireland’s only inhabited offshore island, a place where dramatic cliffs, rich history and a slower pace of life come together. Just six miles off the Antrim coast and around 25 minutes by ferry from Ballycastle, it feels like another world with dramatic cliffs, wildflower-lined country roads, and rare flora and fauna.

Home to Northern Ireland’s largest seabird colony, Rathlin is one of the best places in the country to see puffins, with the main season running from late April to July. Beyond the birds, you can follow scenic walking routes along quiet country roads lined with wildflowers, visit lighthouses perched on the edge of the Atlantic, and keep an eye out for seals and dolphins around the coast.

Whether you’re coming for the wildlife, the stories of the island’s past or simply the chance to breathe out, you’ll find a warm welcome from the small island community who call Rathlin home. Use the guides below to plan what to see and do, where to stay and where to eat.

## Things to See and Do in Rathlin

Rathlin Island sits just six miles off the County Antrim coast. A peaceful haven for nature lovers, history buffs and anyone seeking a slower pace, it feels a world away from the rest of Northern Ireland despite being just a 25-minute ferry ride from Ballycastle.

It's home to [RSPB Rathlin Seabird Centre](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/rspb-rathlin-west-light-seabird-centre/70692101/), situated at the island's West Lighthouse, where thousands of puffins, guillemots, razorbills and other seabirds nest on the cliffs from late April to July. The lighthouse is dramatic in its own right, perched on the cliff edge with a unique "upside-down" design, and the journey there by foot, bike or minibus is part of the experience in itself. For local history, visit the [Rathlin Boathouse Visitor Centre](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/rathlin-island-boathouse-visitors-centre/67495101/) or seek out Bruce's Cave, a site linked to the legend of Robert the Bruce and the legend of the spider.

## Where to Stay on Rathlin Island

Whether you're after rustic charm or coastal comfort, Rathlin has a small but welcoming choice of places to stay. [The Manor House](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/manor-house-country-hotel/67911101/), a historic Georgian building overlooking the harbour, offers elegant rooms and stunning sea views. You'll also find a number of cosy B&Bs and self-catering cottages across the island, which are ideal for unwinding after a day of exploring. Booking ahead is recommended, especially during puffin season and the summer months when the island is most popular with visitors.

## Where to Eat and Drink on Rathlin Island

When it comes to food and drink, Rathlin keeps things simple but satisfying. The [Belleek Restaurant at the Manor House](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/belleek-restaurant-at-manor-house-country-hotel/68751101/) serves hearty favourites alongside its speciality seafood, all with a warm island welcome. For something more traditional, [McCuaig’s Bar](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/mccuaigs-bar/96139101/) is a favourite with locals and visitors alike, with pub classics, fresh seafood and the opportunity for a cosy pint by the fire. Before you catch the ferry home, pick up some homemade treats from the island shop.

Whether you come for a day or stay longer, Rathlin rewards you at your own pace. Plan your visit and start your island adventure today.

## When Is the Best Time to See Puffins on Rathlin Island?

The best time to see puffins on Rathlin Island is from late April to early July, with late May and June often the most rewarding. This is when the birds are back on the cliffs, settling into their burrows and, once the chicks hatch, flying in and out with beakfuls of fish. The best place to see them is the [RSPB Rathlin Seabird Centre](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/rspb-rathlin-west-light-seabird-centre/70692101/), which overlooks Northern Ireland's largest seabird colony.

### Puffin Season on Rathlin at a Glance:

- **Late March to April:** The first puffins typically return around the end of March, with more arriving through April. The seabird centre usually reopens around Easter.
- **Late April to early July:** Peak viewing. The cliffs are packed with puffins, razorbills, guillemots and kittiwakes, and the noise is part of the show.
- **Mid to late July:** The colony starts to empty as birds head back out to sea. Razorbills and guillemots tend to leave first, with puffins close behind.
- **August to March:** The puffins are out in the open ocean and the seabird centre is closed for the winter.

### Where to See Puffins on Rathlin Island

The seabird centre sits at the island's West Lighthouse, around 4.5 miles from the harbour. The viewing platform is reached by a flight of 98 steps down the cliff, and RSPB staff are on hand to help you spot and identify what you're looking at. To get there, you can walk, hire a bike or take one of the minibuses that run from the harbour. If you're walking with a dog, note that dogs aren't allowed in Kebble Nature Reserve, which you pass through on the way.

### Tips for Spotting Puffins

- Check the [RSPB Seabird Centre](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/rspb-rathlin-west-light-seabird-centre/70692101/)'s opening dates before you travel, as they change from year to year. Hours are usually 9am to 5pm, with last entry at 4pm.
- Wear sturdy footwear and bring a windproof layer. The steps and cliff paths are steep and exposed.
- Be patient. Puffins are wild birds, so sightings can't be guaranteed, but the colony is busy enough that most visitors are rewarded.
- Also keep an ear out around Church Bay between mid-April and early July for the corncrake, a rare and elusive bird that can occasionally be spotted.

generation_excerpts: Rathlin Island is Northern Ireland’s only inhabited offshore island, a place where dramatic cliffs, rich history and a slower pace of life come together. Just six miles off the Antrim coast and around 25 minutes by ferry from Ballycastle, it feels like another world with dramatic cliffs, wildflower-lined country roads, and rare flora and fauna.

Home to Northern Ireland’s largest seabird colony, Rathlin is one of the best places in the country to see puffins, with the main season running from late April to July. Beyond the birds, you can follow scenic walking routes along quiet country roads lined with wildflowers, visit lighthouses perched on the edge of the Atlantic, and keep an eye out for seals and dolphins around the coast.
